looks.text: PRUITT, in a child's paint. The flag's up. Nobody has come for the mail.
The Pruitts, in frames off the gas station's own rack. Earl in his red cap in every one, grinning like he's won something. Marcy has her arm through his. Two children, squinting into the sun.
Crayon drawings under magnets. A tall brown shape among the trees, waving. In a child's letters: DADDYS FRIEND.
A county map, pinned and re-pinned. Earl's sightings in red ink, every one dated. Beside a few of them, in blue, in another hand: I saw it too.
Two small beds, made. A torch is gone from its hook by the door. The window is open, and there's a chair pulled up under it.
Pencil marks up the door frame, a date beside each. The highest is from this spring.
